hook: SCP-1422 is a short, dry report about a gap in the Foundation's own knowledge that went unnoticed for a very long time. The anomaly concerns a famous real-world national park, and part of the fun is how completely ordinary that place is. Read the evidence list carefully, since the joke and the chill come from the same details.
whyItMatters: It is an anomaly defined entirely by absence: no object, no entity, only a hole in what an entire organization knows. The file leans into a worry that runs through many entries, namely that the Foundation might be unable to perceive its own blind spots. Its Neutralized classification, and the doubts attached to it, keep it unsettling long after the last line.
thingsToNotice: The evidence is presented like a social survey, with purchase records and browser histories, which makes the absurd premise feel bureaucratically real. The discovery happens almost by accident, through a junior researcher's vacation memory written up after time spent inside another anomaly. Each hypothesis in the second addendum is more uncomfortable than the one before, ending with the possibility that someone wanted the park hidden. The final addendum admits the effect may simply have moved on to something else, which turns the reader's own certainty into the next question.

related.note: Named in the hypotheses as a possible route to countering effects like this one.
A well-known antimemetic entry about something the Foundation cannot hold in memory.
